https://www.grimsbytelegraph.co.uk/news/.text: A "hidden gem" North Lincolnshire pub will have its time in the limelight next week when it appears on popular teatime show Four in a Bed. Vicky Horsewood, who runs the Nelthorpe Arms in South Ferriby, will appear with staff member Anne Marie Stockdale in the show, where public house and bed and breakfast owners battle it out each night to provide the best guest experience of the week. Vicky, who has been involved in running the pub for 25 years, was approached by Channel 4 who asked if she would like to take part. She runs the South Ferriby pub with Vicky Allington. Vicky Allington stayed at home while Vicky Horsewood and Anne Marie took part in the show, which sees owners staying in each other's establishments and rating them each day for cleanliness, hospitality, facilities, sleep quality and - of course - breakfast. At the end of the stay, guests pay what they consider a fair price for their visit by leaving cash in an envelope. At the end of the week, a winner is crowned based on these scores. Vicky said: "It’s a hidden gem, with lots of regulars and we are the heart of the village. I like to think we made friends, we all got along well. I love my job. I love my pub. I wouldn’t keep coming back after 25 years if I didn’t love the place. I love the customers, they are like family." The two Vickys will host a screening party every day in the pub from 4.30pm starting on Monday 21 September. Four in a Bed will be shown on Channel 4 and the Nelthorpe Arms will be the first of the week to feature. On Monday's show the week's contestants will be hosted there. At the end of the week, the pub will put on a disco for visitors after the winner has been announced on Friday's show. The pub has six rooms and attracts guests from all over the world, with travellers from the USA, Australia, Italy and Poland among their recent guests. Former guests have responded to the pub's social media announcement about their time on the show, saying they will try to watch from all corners of the globe. The pub also welcomes campers who want to park up for the night in the car park, as long as they make themselves known and stop in for a drink or some food. Four in a Bed airs on Channel 4 at 5pm every day from Monday 21 September to Friday 26 September. https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world.text: Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX, is an internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted it for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed by the US Pentagon for government and military missions. Unveiled in 2022, Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the US department of defence. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology and the distinction is not always clear-cut. Starshield's secure services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone. Musk, who was Trump’s efficiency tsar early into the president’s second term, pushed back on criticism of his Starlink service on Wednesday, writing on social media: “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX.” Any limits on the speed or usage of Starshield would be decided by the US military or the president, he added.

Log in here » SOFIA, Bulgaria (AP) — Bulgaria on Wednesday said Russia was likely behind drone attacks that struck four ships in the Black Sea in the past week, sinking two, but there was no way of proving Moscow’s culpability. Rescuers are still searching for 11 crew members missing after drone strikes on Tuesday sank two ships in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone and adjacent waters, while five other crew members were rescued. One of the ships is registered to Guinea-Bissau but the other one, the Chelsea-3, is Ukrainian-owned, registered in Odesa and sails under the flag of Malta, a European Union member. Four of the saved sailors from the drone-attacked and sunk ship HS Dignity seen on emergency rescue tug of Bulgarian Navy's - Mizar as they are transported to the port of Varna, Bulgaria, late Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026. (Moreto.net via AP) “There is no logic in Ukraine attacking its own ships and crews, given that the outcome of all these attacks favors Russia — and indeed, the logic points in that direction. The problem is that we cannot prove it,” Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told Parliament. Radev on Tuesday summoned the Russian ambassador to Sofia, who said she does not have any information from the Russian defense ministry but she did not rule out the possibility that “these attacks represent a provocation by a third party.” The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Dignity sank Tuesday after it was hit by a military strike. Four sailors, three Syrian nationals and one Egyptian, were rescued and arrived in the port of Varna, district Gov. Mario Smarkov said. “All four appeared to be in relatively good condition and had sustained no injuries,” he said. A fifth sailor is expected to arrive later on Wednesday. Smarkov said the search for the 11 missing crew members continues. Bulgaria has requested international assistance for the investigation into attacks on commercial vessels, as well as NATO support to strengthen surveillance and control systems and response capabilities against drone attacks. President Iliana Yotova called for an immediate halt to hostilities in the Black Sea and a moratorium on drone attacks against commercial and civilian infrastructure, following the latest drone attacks. “The unprecedented attacks demonstrate that the war has reached the Black Sea and that the conflict is intensifying,” Yotova said in a TV interview on Tuesday. She explained that coordinated steps have been taken with her colleagues from Romania and Turkey in the wake of the growing risks and dangers in the Black Sea basin. In a separate incident, Radev confirmed an attack on Starlink antennas near the capital, Sofia, but did not elaborate citing an ongoing investigation. Radev, who was answering questions in Parliament about the attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea, was asked by opposition lawmakers about details of an alleged arson of communication devices with the Starlink satellite system on Tuesday. “The investigation is being worked on with partner services and is extremely intensive, with a result expected soon,” Radev said, adding that any “premature disclosure could hinder the investigation.” Opposition MPs posted on social media that two masked men deliberately set fire to 11 of the 17 antennas used to connect to SpaceX’s Starlink satellite system at a site in the Sofia area.
